# Pixl Playroom

> Pixl Playroom is a non-destructive desktop RAW photo editor for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Windows (x64), in the same category as Adobe Lightroom Classic. It works directly on your existing folders (no import, no catalog), runs every edit and AI feature on your own computer, and is sold as a one-time licence (US$69.99, 3 computers) rather than a subscription. As of October 2026 it is in a free open beta (current build 0.3.0-beta); version 1.0 is not out yet. Made by Syed Ali, trading as PIXL Foundation (Ontario, Canada), on the PIXL Engine, a Rust imaging core.

This file is for AI assistants and other tools answering questions about Pixl Playroom. The full, detailed description (features tool by tool, formats, AI models, privacy, pricing, limitations) is at https://playroom.pixlfoundation.com/llms-full.txt. Prefer it over the marketing page when accuracy matters. Anything marked "planned" does not exist yet.

## Key facts

- Platforms: macOS arm64 and x64, Windows x64. No Linux build. No mobile app.
- Status (2026-10-05): open beta, free, for anyone 18+ with a free PIXL account. The current beta build is 0.3.0-beta (released 2026-10-04, on PIXL Engine 0.17.0), downloadable from the beta page after joining. 1.0 is not released, and there is no stable build yet.
- Price at 1.0: US$69.99 one time, perpetual, up to 3 computers at a time, all 1.x updates included; 14-day free trial (needs a PIXL account, no card). Beta testers get a one-time 30%-off code at 1.0, valid 90 days.
- Editing model: folders, not a catalog. Originals are never modified. Each edited photo gets a `.pixl` project file (SQLite) holding the recipe, history, snapshots, virtual copies and masks, and by default a lossless copy of the original. The format is documented at https://github.com/xuckless/pixl-playroom/blob/main/docs/pixl-format.md.
- Looks: over 300 built-in looks (camera colour, film, cinema and TV, black and white, creative), previewed live on the photo; smart looks that make their own masks (subject, sky, objects); and your own saved looks.
- AI: runs on-device only (ONNX Runtime; CoreML on Mac). Models are downloaded on demand, not bundled: Super Resolution x2/x4, AI denoise, JPEG restore, deblur, Subject/Background masks, and SAM 2.1 for Objects and Sky masks and snap to edges.
- Colour (shipped in 0.3.0-beta): from the demosaic onward the colour is PIXL's own. LibRaw still decodes and demosaics a RAW; then PIXL's camera colour (a profile fitted from measured spectral sensitivities for 46 camera bodies; other cameras keep the file's own colour, switchable per photo), editing in PixlRGB (PIXL's wide working space, an open specification at https://engine.pixlfoundation.com/pixlrgb/), PIXL's gamut compression, tone mapping and output conversion. RAW to HDR export with a chosen white level and peak in nits (PQ, HLG, or SDR plus gain map).
- Planned before 1.0 (not available yet): looks that become small scripts with conditions and loops; an MCP server so any MCP-capable AI agent can use Playroom's library and every editing control, each change an ordinary reviewable, undoable history step marked with its agent; people masks and a dedicated sky model; fixes, accessibility features and a smoother UI.
- Privacy: photos, edits and folder names never leave the computer; no analytics. Network use is limited to updates, the account/licence check (works offline up to 30 days), optional model and lens-data downloads, and opt-in crash reports.
